Simulate a classification dataset with label errors

Source: R/simulate.R
simulate_label_noise.Rd

Generates true classes, given labels in which a share of examples have been switched to another class at random, and predicted probabilities from a softmax of noisy logits that favour the true class. Useful for examples, teaching and checking how well the methods recover known errors.

Usage

simulate_label_noise(
  n = 1000,
  n_classes = 4,
  noise_rate = 0.1,
  signal = 2,
  prior = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

n

Number of examples.

n_classes

Number of classes, at least two.

noise_rate

Probability that an example's given label is switched to a different, uniformly chosen class.

signal

How much the logit of the true class is raised. Larger values give a more accurate classifier.

prior

Class probabilities of the true classes. Defaults to a moderately imbalanced distribution.

seed

Optional random seed. The global random number generator is restored afterwards.

Value

A tibble in the yardstick convention with columns true, given (factors) and one .pred_<class> probability column per class.

Examples

sim <- simulate_label_noise(n = 10, seed = 42)
sim
#> # A tibble: 10 × 6
#>    true  given .pred_A .pred_B .pred_C .pred_D
#>    <fct> <fct>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>
#>  1 D     D     0.245   0.0488  0.105   0.602  
#>  2 D     D     0.573   0.00980 0.118   0.300  
#>  3 A     A     0.241   0.110   0.369   0.280  
#>  4 C     C     0.0877  0.390   0.466   0.0560 
#>  5 B     B     0.0168  0.946   0.0319  0.00490
#>  6 B     B     0.224   0.571   0.0213  0.183  
#>  7 C     C     0.141   0.145   0.631   0.0832 
#>  8 A     A     0.0969  0.0320  0.0797  0.791
